children: Boxlight Corporation (Nasdaq: BOXL), a leading provider of integrated education technology solutions, today announced the expansion of its STEM education partnership with Jefferson Parish Schools in Louisiana, providing
more than 200 Robo E4 3D printers, filament, and MyStemKits curriculum access
for science teachers across the district.

The initiative began with the district exploring approximately 50 3D printers for its middle and high school science programs. Through discovery conversations, the project expanded as district leaders identified a need for more than hardware; they were looking for curriculum, professional development, implementation planning, ongoing support, and a true technology partner.
The
Robo E4
printer was selected not only because it is a high-speed machine designed for the rigors of the classroom, but also because it comes bundled with MimioSTEM’s award-winning curriculum solution:
MyStemKits

. This curriculum platform provides standards-driven lessons, activities, design challenges, and ready-to-print 3D models designed to help educators integrate hands-on STEM learning into instruction and make sure that their new 3D printers can be used to their fullest potential.

“We are grateful to Boxlight for investing in our teachers and students in a way that goes beyond simply providing new technology. These resources will give our students more opportunities to create, explore, solve problems and bring what they are learning to life.”
Dr. James Gray, Superintendent, Jefferson Parish Schools

“Our teachers will also have the training, curriculum and support they need to bring these learning experiences into the classroom. When teachers feel prepared and supported, students have more opportunities to engage, grow and see what is possible through STEM.”
Aligning Technology with Instruction

Boxlight worked with district leaders to align MyStemKits resources with Jefferson Parish’s science scope and sequence, helping ensure teachers have relevant instructional materials from the start of implementation.

“In Jefferson Parish Schools, our focus is always on making sure new resources connect directly to what students are learning every day. By aligning the technology with our science curriculum, teachers can introduce hands-on experiences that reinforce key concepts and give students new ways to demonstrate what they know.” -
Laura Roussel, Chief Academic Officer, Jefferson Parish Schools.

During that process, Boxlight identified a need for additional environmental science content and developed new lessons to help address those instructional gaps, demonstrating the company’s commitment to supporting district-specific instructional needs.
Jefferson Parish Schools selected
Bluum

as its reseller to meet the district’s procurement requirements through TIMS. Bluum provided significant support throughout the sales process, including local district engagement, site visits, product demonstrations, and planning and procurement support.

“Jefferson Parish Schools had a clear vision for expanding hands-on STEM learning, and we were proud to support the district as the project evolved from an initial technology discussion into a comprehensive instructional initiative,” said
Kurt Roberts, Client Director, Bluum
. “Working alongside Boxlight, we were able to help connect the district with the technology, curriculum, professional learning, and support needed to make the implementation successful.”
Professional Development and Ongoing Support
Boxlight developed an implementation roadmap that includes teacher training, curriculum integration, ongoing coaching, and continued support throughout the school year.
The rollout will include a customized
week-long professional development program in September
, with multiple Boxlight team members traveling to New Orleans to provide concurrent sessions tailored to teachers’ specific subjects and grade levels.
In addition to the kick-off week of professional learning, Boxlight will also provide various
virtual learning follow-up sessions
for interested educators and has provided a
3D printer certification course
so that both the teachers and their students can become 3D printer certified.
The initiative reflects Boxlight’s approach to education technology:
providing the technology, curriculum, training, and ongoing support needed to turn classroom tools into meaningful instructional experiences.

Jefferson Parish Schools leaders emphasized the importance of communication, curriculum support, product support, and professional learning throughout the planning process. Boxlight’s comprehensive support model is designed to help teachers confidently integrate 3D printing into instruction and use it to engage students in hands-on STEM learning.
“This initiative is a strong example of how understanding a district’s goals can transform a technology purchase into a broader instructional partnership,” said
Jillian Dale, STEM Sales Manager, Boxlight
. “Our goal is to make it easier for educators to confidently use technology to support curriculum and create meaningful learning experiences.”
About Jefferson Parish Schools:

Jefferson Parish Schools is the largest and most diverse public school system in Louisiana. Our system of 74 schools serves approximately 45,000 students on both banks of the Mississippi River. With approximately 6,000 employees, JP Schools is one of the largest employers in Jefferson Parish. Our district exists to provide the education our students deserve to succeed in life and make our world a better place.
About Boxlight Corporation

Boxlight Corporation (Nasdaq: BOXL) is a leading provider of education technology solutions through its award-winning Clevertouch®, FrontRow™, Mimio®, and Boxlight brands. The company develops, sells, and supports a portfolio of instructional software, interactive displays, classroom audio, campus communication, emergency notification, digital signage, STEM solutions, and professional services designed to improve engagement, communication, collaboration, and safety in learning environments worldwide.
